title: A spreading geometrically irreducible affine chart in a generically integral family
statement: Let $X$ be reduced affine, let $S$ be integral affine [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $\eta$ be a generic point of $S$ and suppose $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. There exist an affine open $W\subseteq X$ and an open $U\subseteq S$ containing $\eta$ such that the fibres $W_s$ are geometrically irreducible for all $s\in U$. No density assertion about $W_s\subseteq X_s$ and no irreducibility assertion about $X_s$ is included.

proof.text: Flatness over the domain A embeds the reduced source ring B in its geometrically integral generic fibre. Its function field L is a regular finitely generated extension of K=Frac(A). A separating transcendence basis and a primitive element give an absolutely irreducible minimal polynomial P; clear denominators to put P over A. Take the primitive numerator over K before clearing base denominators. After the monic coordinate change and a base localization, the hypersurface quotient is free over the polynomial ring in the other variables, so it embeds in its generic fibre and is a domain; this justifies the common-function-field comparison in the next step.

The hypersurface ring A[x_1,...,x_(r+1)]/(P) and B have the same generic function field. Express finite generating sets of each ring as fractions in this field and invert the denominators to obtain a common nonempty affine open over a principal open of the base. Its generic fibre is nonempty.

Spread absolute irreducibility of P by Tag 0557. Make P monic in its last variable by a triangular separated-powers substitution and invert its nonzero leading coefficient. For each positive factor-degree pair form the finite type coefficient algebra for bounded-degree monic factors. Nullstellensatz makes its generic fibre zero, so inverting a nonzero base element kills it. Invert the product over the finitely many positive pairs to exclude every algebraically closed residue-field factorization.

All hypersurface fibres on this base open are geometrically integral. Their common open has geometrically irreducible fibres wherever nonempty. As the common affine open is flat and finitely presented over the base, its image is open and contains the generic point. Choose a principal base neighbourhood inside this image; restricting the common open along it preserves its affineness in X and ensures nonempty fibres. Dimension zero uses a linear polynomial and an empty product of factor obstructions.

theorem exists_generic_geometrically_integral_affine_chart
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsReduced X] [IsAffine S] [IsIntegral S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (η : S) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η))
    (hred : GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ W : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen W ∧ ∃ U : S.Opens, η ∈ U ∧
      ∀ s, s ∈ U → GeometricallyIrreducible ((W.ι ≫ f).fiberToSpecResidueField s)
